title: Types of Discontinuity: Removable
notes: **Definition:** A removable discontinuity occurs when lim(x→a) f(x) exists but either f(a) is undefined or f(a) ≠ lim(x→a) f(x).
**Key characteristic:** The limit exists (LHL = RHL), but the function value doesn't match or isn't defined.
**Removable aspect:** The discontinuity can be 'removed' by redefining f(a) to equal the limit value.
**Condition:** lim(x→a) f(x) exists but lim(x→a) f(x) ≠ f(a), or f(a) is not defined.
**Graphical appearance:** A hole or gap in the graph at x = a, with the curve approaching the same point from both sides.
**Example:** f(x) = (x²-4)/(x-2) has a removable discontinuity at x = 2 (hole at (2,4)).
**Fix:** Define f(2) = 4 to make the function continuous at x = 2.
**Distinction:** Different from jump and infinite discontinuities where the limit doesn't exist.
confusion: Don't confuse removable discontinuities with jump discontinuities — in removable cases, the limit exists.
A hole in the graph doesn't always mean removable — check if LHL = RHL first.
Removable doesn't mean 'easily fixed' — it refers to the mathematical property that redefining one point creates continuity.
Don't confuse with infinite discontinuities where the limit approaches ±∞.
The function may be undefined at the point, but that alone doesn't guarantee removability — the limit must exist.
practice: Show that f(x) = (x²-4)/(x-2) has a removable discontinuity at x = 2 and define f(2) to make it continuous.
For f(x) = sin(x)/x, identify the removable discontinuity and define f(0) appropriately.
Determine if g(x) = {x² for x≠1, 3 for x=1} has a removable discontinuity at x = 1.
Find all removable discontinuities of h(x) = (x³-1)/(x-1).
Explain why f(x) = 1/x has a non-removable discontinuity at x = 0.
universalFacts: Removable discontinuities are the 'mildest' type of discontinuity — they can be fixed by redefinition.
In complex analysis, removable singularities have special significance in function theory.
Many apparent discontinuities in formulas turn out to be removable upon simplification.
The concept extends to higher dimensions where removable singularities are studied in several complex variables.
In numerical analysis, understanding removable discontinuities helps avoid computational errors.
